title: Congressional Calls to Abolish H-1B Program Grow as Vance Fraud Crackdown Escalates
excerpt: Republican lawmakers are pushing beyond reform toward outright abolition of the H-1B visa program, as Vice President Vance's fraud task force triggers an aggressive federal investigation with search warrants already being prepared.
body:
What began as a fraud investigation has rapidly evolved into a broader political assault on one of America's most consequential immigration programs — with Indian professionals squarely in the crosshairs.

Vice President JD Vance's Task Force to Eliminate Fraud has triggered a sweeping probe by the Department of Labor's Office of Inspector General into the H-1B visa and PERM labor certification systems. DOL Inspector General Anthony D'Esposito told the New York Post that his team is already "in the process of writing up affidavits to swear out search warrants," signaling criminal enforcement actions may be imminent.

Beyond Fraud: A Push to Scrap the Program

The political conversation in Washington has shifted beyond cleaning up fraud. Republican lawmakers are now openly discussing abolishing the H-1B program altogether.

Microsoft Xbox Layoffs Become a Flashpoint

The political momentum has been fueled by corporate decisions that critics say prove the program's worst tendencies. Microsoft's Xbox division laid off approximately 1,600 workers last week — even as the parent company had been approved for 2,273 H-1B visas this year. The juxtaposition drew viral outrage and gave ammunition to those arguing the program displaces American workers rather than filling genuine skills gaps.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=xtUCfSkimN8

The DOL investigation has singled out IT consulting firm Cognizant by name, with D'Esposito telling reporters that whistleblowers had raised concerns. Sources cited by the New York Post suggest many major tech companies rely on thousands of H-1B visas "as a way to cut costs."

D'Esposito has framed the issue in stark terms, calling it "the exploitation of vulnerable workers, forced labor, the displacement of American workers, and abusive human trafficking."

Legal and Legislative Fronts

A federal judge struck down the Trump administration's $100,000 supplemental fee on certain new H-1B visa petitions in June, ruling it amounted to a tax only Congress could impose. The setback may push the administration toward working with Congress on legislative solutions. House Budget Committee Chairman Jodey Arrington (R-TX) has indicated that anti-fraud initiatives are providing strong returns, and Republicans are exploring additional funding for fraud prevention technology in upcoming spending bills.

"We shipped all our manufacturing jobs overseas and people were told to 'learn how to code.' Well, now they're being replaced with the H-1B visa workers on the coding jobs as well. So when is the American worker actually going to get a win here?"

— Rep. Riley Moore (R-W.Va.)

Indian Professionals Face Mounting Uncertainty

For the Indian diaspora, these developments carry outsized consequences. Indian nationals receive approximately 70% of all approved H-1B petitions, and combined with Chinese nationals, the two groups account for over 80% of recipients. There are currently an estimated 730,000 H-1B visa holders in the United States, with 65% employed at tech companies.

The shift from targeted fraud enforcement to calls for program abolition represents a qualitative escalation. Previous administrations adjusted H-1B rules, raised fees, or tightened eligibility. The current political climate — with an active criminal investigation, bipartisan frustration over corporate layoffs, and a vocal congressional bloc advocating elimination — creates a fundamentally different threat to the program's future. For Indian tech professionals on H-1B visas or hoping to obtain one, the coming months will be critical.
